name: Hardcoded absolute file paths
description: Java applications with hardcoded absolute file paths fail in containers as the directory structure differs from development environments.
remediation: Use relative paths or environment variables to configure file paths. Load resources from the classpath when possible.

name: Hardcoded server hostnames
description: Applications with hardcoded hostnames like 'localhost' or specific IP addresses fail in container environments where service discovery mechanisms should be used instead.
remediation: Use environment variables or configuration files to define service endpoints. In Kubernetes, use service names for discovery.

name: Fixed server ports
description: Applications with hardcoded server ports cannot adapt to port mappings in container environments, leading to connectivity issues.
remediation: Make server port configurable via environment variables or configuration files.

name: Local filesystem storage
description: Applications that store data locally (file uploads, temp files, etc.) lose this data when containers restart or scale.
remediation: Use volume mounts for persistent data or migrate to cloud storage services/databases for stateful data.

examples.before:
File uploadDir = new File("/app/uploads");
File uploadedFile = new File(uploadDir, fileName);

name: Log files written to local filesystem
description: Applications writing logs to the local filesystem lose log data when containers are terminated.
remediation: Configure logging to output to stdout/stderr for container log collection.

name: Static configuration files
description: Applications relying on static configuration files baked into the application cannot adapt to dynamic container environments.
remediation: Externalize configurations using environment variables or Spring profiles.

examples.before:
Properties props = new Properties();
props.load(new FileInputStream("config.properties"));
examples.after:
String dbUrl = System.getenv("DB_URL");
String dbUser = System.getenv("DB_USER");

name: Fixed JVM memory settings
description: Java applications with fixed JVM heap settings that don't account for container memory limits can cause out-of-memory issues.
remediation: Use percentage-based memory settings or container-aware JVM options (Java 10+).

name: Database filesystem access
description: Applications that access local database files directly (H2, SQLite) lose data when containers restart.
remediation: Use external database services or persistent volumes for database files.

name: OS-specific commands execution
description: Applications that execute OS-specific commands using Runtime.exec() may fail in containers.
remediation: Include required binaries in the container image or refactor to use Java libraries.

examples.after: // Include ImageMagick in Dockerfile or use Java image libraries

name: Missing health check endpoints
description: Applications lacking health check endpoints hinder container orchestrators from managing application lifecycle.
remediation: Implement health check endpoints using Spring Boot Actuator or custom endpoints.
